argument:
The bear is right that a good business is not automatically an attractively priced stock. Still, the case includes delivered comparable growth, strong cash generation, lower year-ago debt and price above both medium and long averages; among this set, those are multiple positive observations rather than only a lagging long average.

Cooling MACD and unresolved settlement approval temper timing, but do not erase the trend or cash economics. I concede valuation protection remains unproved. The defensible bullish position is a measured trend-and-quality candidate with patience on entry, not a claim that sizing substitutes for expected-return evidence.
key_points: Medium and long trends remain positive
No verified bargain or resolved-litigation assumption
rebuttal_to_previous: Concede valuation and settlement gaps; independent operating/cash and medium-term trend evidence supports relative candidacy despite cooling momentum.
